item.description: LaNorris Sellers (left) of the South Carolina Gamecocks drops back to pass in the first half Nov. 7, 2026 against the Texas A&M Aggies at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, South Carolina. (Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) Take a look at the box score of the 17-9 road loss for Texas A&M football to No. 21 South Carolina and you'd be forgiven for being a little perplexed. On paper, the Aggies performed well. They put up 457 yards to the Gamecocks 360, rushed for 206 yards to the hosts' 109, possessed the ball for almost 10 more minutes and - for just the second time this season against a Power Four opponent - did not turn the ball over. David Olano of the Texas A&M Aggies kicks a field goal in the first half Nov. 7, 2026 against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, South Carolina. (Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) Yet in what has become a familiar pattern this year, A&M was unable to score a single touchdown, putting up just nine points as the Aggies fell to 4-5 on the year and just 1-5 in Southeastern Conference play. A&M is the first team in NCAA history to have more than 450 total yards of offense, zero turnovers, and score zero touchdowns in the same game, according to TexAgs. "(We) gave a lot of stuff away," head coach Mike Elko said. "You can't get down there as much as we did and not come away with points when you're playing a team like that. … But at the end of the day, we had a chance to win a game in the fourth quarter, and we didn't do it." Success on the ground Running back Reubem Owens II entered this season as the Aggies' RB1, but had fallen down the depth chart as the year went on behind freshman KJ Edwards and sophomore Jamarion Morrow. But with Edwards recovering from the flu and Morrow - who recorded just one carry - banged up, according to Elko, Owens seemed to play as if he wanted to regain that RB1 title. On the Aggies' first play from scrimmage, Owens scampered 40 yards downfield to give A&M an explosive start to the day. "I just had a good week," Owens said. " … I felt it before the game that it was going to be one of the ones. Coach gave me the opportunity and my O-line gave me the opportunity, and I put it out there." By halftime, Owens led the Aggies with 64 yards on 10 carries as the Aggies picked up 101 yards on the ground - a number made even more impressive by A&M's defense, which held South Carolina to just 36 rushing yards in the first half. "We challenged them to be physical," Elko said. "I thought that was going to be a big part of that game. They're a really good run offense, they're a really good run defense. item.description: Fans celebrate goal against their own team in Série B 🇧🇷 Náutico fans were at the center of an unusual scene during the team's match against CRB this Saturday (7), in the penultimate round of Série B. The game took place at Aflitos stadium, home of Timbu, but the home fans celebrated the goals scored by...the opposition! The reason is the local rivalry: Sport are competing directly with CRB for promotion to the first division. With Náutico no longer having anything to play for in the league, the fans celebrated a result that hurt their rivals, as CRB won 3–0. And it wasn't just the fans who showed little interest in Saturday's game. On Thursday (5), Náutico's board decided to send nine players, including regular starters, on holiday early. item.title: Justin Gaethje’s manager shuts down Ilia Topuria rematch: ‘Will never happen!’
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - MAY 06: (L-R) Ilia Topuria and Justin Gaethje face off on the South Lawn in front of the White House on May 06, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Zuffa LLC) The fans want a Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria rematch. Ilia Topuria wants it. The UFC wants it. But Justin Gaethje does not, according to his manager Ali Abdelaziz. Gaethje took the UFC lightweight title off Topuria in a brutal war on the White House lawn back in June, forcing Topuria’s corner to throw in the towel after the fourth round. Few had given Justin a chance of winning, and now “The Highlight” seems uninterested in giving Ilia a chance to win that fight back. Topuria just did a media blitz of interviews, and a big topic of discussion was a potential Gaethje rematch. Topuria put up a poll on social media to ask his fans who they’d rather see him face off against. After 24 hours, Justin Gaethje edged out Paddy Pimblett, 474,000 votes to 385,000. Alas, there continues to be no interest in the fight from Gaethje’s side. 🚨‼️Ali Abdelaziz completely shuts down the possibility of an Ilia Topuria rematch 👀 🗣️“This rematch will never happen, and I agree with him. His brother saved his life. It's very hard to come back from the trauma of a fight like that. I've seen Justin do this to many people,… pic.twitter.com/WxwASLAyfQ — FightLuck (@FightluckBet) November 8, 2026 “This rematch will never happen,” Gaethje’s manager Ali Abdelaziz tweeted and later deleted. Abdelaziz also referred to a quote from Topuria thanking his brother for stopping the fight after the fourth round. “I agree with him – his brother saved his life,” Abdelaziz wrote. “It’s very hard to come back from the trauma of a fight like that. I’ve seen Justin do this to many people, and coming back wasn’t easy for them. Wishing him the best of luck.” Gaethje continues to flirt with retirement and has said he won’t come back unless it’s for a massive fight. And while the Topuria rematch certainly qualifies, it’s also a fight he won in dominant fashion. There’s no way for him to improve on the performance he gave on the White House lawn against Topuria, so why go back and do it again immediately? ‘Because it’d be awesome,’ is the obvious answer. But Gaethje is looking to wrap his career up on his terms, not be the foil in Ilia Topuria’s comeback story. If Abdelaziz is giving us a legit look into Gaethje’s mindset and not just posturing as a negotiation tactic, we’ll have to resign ourselves to … Gaethje vs. Tsarukyan or Volkanovski? Not the worst consolation prizes.

item.title: Georgia Crushes Ole Miss While Ohio State Crashes Out
item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Georgia Bulldogs defensive back KJ Bolden (4) and defensive back Demello Jones (8) react during the first half against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Georgia football obliterated Ole Miss 42-7 on Saturday to end a 16-game home winning streak for the Rebels. The Bulldogs rolled past their SEC rivals in Oxford and put themselves back in the hunt for the number one spot. This win comes right after No. 1 Miami lost to Notre Dame, clearing the path for Georgia to climb back to the top of the US LBM Coaches Poll. Quarterback Gunner Stockton looked sharp even though he threw the ball fewer times than usual. He completed nine of 15 passes for 186 yards and tossed four touchdowns against the Rebels. Wide receiver Talyn Taylor caught three of those scores, including a massive 58-yard strike that sparked the rout. The running game was just as deadly, with Nate Frazier gaining 107 yards on 16 carries to wear down the Ole Miss defense. Georgia’s defense held star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss to just 170 passing yards with no touchdowns and one interception. Ohio State’s Playoff Hopes Fade While Georgia soared, Ohio State hit the floor hard with a home loss to Oregon. The Buckeyes now have two straight defeats, and their chances for the College Football Playoff look like they are toast. Per Yahoo Sports, the AP voters will drop Ohio State in the rankings after the Buckeyes were handled at home by Oregon. This follows a previous loss to USC, leaving Ryan Day’s team with a shaky resume despite wins against Iowa and Indiana. The collapse of Ohio State highlights how fast things can change in college football. Teams that look strong in September can crater by November if they lose key games. The Buckeyes are now in a spot where they need to win out just to stay relevant. Meanwhile, Georgia used their own loss to Auburn as a reset to become the most complete team in the country. They have turned back into a dominant force when it matters most. The New Order at the Top With Miami’s loss and Georgia’s win, the top of the polls is set for a major shakeup. Following their Holy War victory over BYU, Utah holds a perfect 9-0 record, marking the first top-10 clash in the series history. The Utes are now one of the last two unbeaten teams left in the nation and are locked in for the Big 12 title game. Per Yahoo Sports, Utah could rise to No. 2 in the coaches poll while UCLA moves to No. 3 after staying perfect. Notre Dame also secured its spot in the playoff chase by beating Miami 31-24 in South Bend. By executing a critical red zone stop with less than four minutes remaining, the Fighting Irish prevented a devastating defeat. They now look forward to Boston College, SMU, and Syracuse to end the year.

item.title: Dolphins fan confidence remains high despite losses
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Michael Taaffe #16 of the Miami Dolphins celebrates during the first half of the game against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the New England Patriots last weekend, dropping to 1-6 and reminding everyone this is a rebuilding year. They held a 13-3 halftime lead against their AFC East rivals, but couldn’t sustain the momentum in the second half and let New England storm back for a 24-19 win. This year is about the growth and development of the team, not necessarily about the wins and losses – but wins sure feel much better than losses. In Week 9, the Dolphins host the Detroit Lions, a 5-2 team that is looking to return to the playoffs in 2026 after missing out last year. A physical team that gets after their opponents each and every week, Detroit serves as an example of the success a philosophy change and roster rebuild can bring. The Lions are five years ahead of Miami on the rebuild path. The FanDuel Sportsbook oddsmakers , expect Detroit to use that advantage to come away with the win on Sunday. The Lions are a 6.5-point favorite for the game. Dolphins fan confidence Despite the losses mounting, Dolphins fans seem to see the course laid out by general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley. Both in their first year in the roles, they have been deliberate in how they reset the Dolphins’ salary cap, roster, and play style. They have the players believing in them, and the fans seem to also trust them. Each week, we ask you to weigh in on how you are feeling about the direction of the Dolphins. We then track the results of our SB Nation Reacts surveys to see how the fan base is feeling about the team, and how it changes over the course of the season. This year, the fans have consistently demonstrated their trust for the new management team and in the direction of the franchise. That doesn’t mean the losses don’t affect fans’ feelings. Heading into last week, 97 percent of fans thought Miami was headed in the right direction, nearing an all-time high after the team’s win over the New York Jets. After the loss to the New England Patriots in Week 8, and as they prepare to face the Detroit Lions in Week 9, fan confidence dropped somewhat, but support for the team remains overwhelming. After 97 percent of respondents said they felt positive about the Dolphins’ direction in Week 8, that number slipped to 86 percent in Week 9. item.title: Meadowbrook volleyball headed back to OHSSA Final Four after regional title
item.description: CAMBRIDGE — To the untrained eye, the Meadowbrook Colts make volleyball look effortless. But behind their nearly flawless sweeps and staggering postseason run lies a simple, sweat-soaked truth: perfection is just the byproduct of the amount of hard work that is put forth. Sweeping past Frankfort Adena (25-16, 25-21, 25-16) in the OHSAA Division V regional championship game on Saturday, November 7, the Meadowbrook Colts captured their second consecutive Final Four appearance, and their third in a remarkable seven-year run of reaching the OHSAA regionals. A record-breaking postseason run With the victory, the Colts improve to 25-1 overall and have now rattled off nine consecutive set wins during their current postseason surge−adding to a dominating performance where they dropped just four sets total during the regular season. Next up for Meadowbrook is an OHSAA State Semifinal matchup against Coldwater on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026 at 11:30 a.m. at the Pam Evans Smith Arena on the campus of Wittenberg University in Springfield, Ohio. Trusting the process While the Colts' play on the volleyball court can make their success look routine, veteran senior Kara Lauder knows the blueprint behind reaching that success. "Our success really comes down to repetition on from a lot of hard work, and being both mentally and physically ready to perform," Launder explained following Thursday's Division V regional semifinal victory over Martins Ferry. "We rep it every single day in practice, so when we get to the game it all just seems to come together for us." Balanced attack fuels success That hard work translates directly into a balanced stat sheet with plenty of contributions from a variety of players. "Sophomore Addie Schultice powered the Colts' attack with 11 kills, 12 points, and 14 digs. Freshman setter Bricelynn Vargeson handed out 41 assists along with 13 digs and two points. Senior Natalee Norman contributed 13 points, 12 kills, and 16 digs, while senior Lyla Thompson chipped in with eight kills, 11 points and three blocks. Junior Presleigh Valentine finished with eight kills, nine points and a pair of digs. Eyes on history For head coach Kelly Zehnder, returning to the state's biggest stage is the validation of a culture built over years of sustained success. "We feel good to get back where we want to be−the Final Four with an opportunity to make school history by doing something that's not been done yet," Zehnder said. "That opportunity before us is great, and our girls deserve it with their hard work and dedication." Looking forward to the challenges awaiting them during next weekend's Final Four, Zehnder emphasized her team's competitive hunger. "Certainly every year feels good, and we are proud of what we have done this season," Zehnder added. "But we know we are going to face some really good competition when we get to the Dayton-Springfield area next weekend. But we are looking forward to being tested by some of the best volleyball teams in the state.

item.title: 'That's Reece' - World Cup semi-final brings out best and worst of Walsh
item.description: On a fractious night in Sydney, it was no surprise to see Reece Walsh at the centre of the action – for better or worse. The full-back scored three of Australia's eight tries as they beat Samoa 44-12 to reach a 16th successive men's Rugby League World Cup final. His two second-half tries helped keep a burgeoning Samoa comeback at bay, while his first-half effort demonstrated his skill and showmanship. On 32 minutes, Walsh administered the harshest of punishments on Samoa for the smallest amount of defensive laxity, racing through the tiniest gap on the left to score. In front of approximately 40,000 spectators, the Kangaroos' number one celebrated with a backflip. It was the kind of celebration you expect from a man once christened by Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys as "the Justin Bieber of rugby league" and "charisma on steroids". But while thrilling the fans, it gives kittens to those in charge. Walsh lost his boot during the flip; when sitting down to put it back on, TV commentators fretted he had injured himself. Australia coach Kevin Walters pointedly said there would be no backflips in the second half during a half-time interview – and indeed Walsh reined himself in. "That's just Reece," Walters told the post-match media conference. "He always brings up something you don't expect. "The backflip was no different. Impressive though. He did it for some sick kids. They all asked him to do a backflip if he scored a try, so you can't really be against that when he's putting a smile on kids' faces." 'Catching the high ball is difficult' Walsh has scored five tries in three matches at this tournament [Getty Images] More concerning for Walters will be the mistakes Walsh made as he got swept up in the feverish atmosphere. Two minutes before Walsh's first try, Samoa's Stephen Crichton appeared to have grounded to close the score to 16-6 after Francis Manuleleua had beaten the Aussie full-back to a high ball. A slow-motion replay led to the debatable conclusion Manuleleua had knocked on. Whether the correct call or not, it was a massive let-off for Walsh. Samoa began to lose their heads soon after, with a major flashpoint coming after Walsh was ruled to have been dangerously tackled. It was Walsh himself who instigated the ruck after the incident. Walsh quickly responded after both Samoan scores, keeping them at arm's length while scoring his first international hat-trick. He needed to after the first one, as Crichton did get his try in the second half after Walsh dropped a bomb. Magic and mistakes go hand in hand, which is the risk Walters has taken by preferring Walsh at full-back to James Tedesco - who was player of the match as he helped Sydney Roosters win last month's NRL Grand Final. item.title: ‘Clean house. This is embarrassing’: Former Ohio State players blast Ryan Day and Buckeyes after loss to Oregon
item.description: Oct 8, 2022; East Lansing, Michigan, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (2) helmet and gloves during warm-ups before the NCAA Division I football game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and Michigan State Spartans at Spartan Stadium. Osu22msu Kwr 14 The Ohio State Buckeyes were embarrassed at home on Saturday, blowing a 14-0 lead in a 41-28 loss to Oregon at Ohio Stadium. It was the team’s second straight loss and third of the season, and it likely ended any hope of a College Football Playoff run. Not surprisingly, plenty of former Buckeyes were furious about what they saw. Several former Ohio State players took to social media during and after the game to rip the team’s performance, with some even calling for major changes in Columbus. Another Ohio State Loss Ohio State’s problems have been building for weeks. The Buckeyes barely escaped Indiana with a 19-15 win on Oct. 17, a game in which starting quarterback Julian Sayin was injured, and then lost 30-18 at USC on Oct. 31 with freshman Luke Fahey under center. Fox’s Joel Klatt was among those critical of the team’s offensive approach, saying of Ohio State’s usage of Jeremiah Smith that “that can’t be your game plan.” On Saturday, Ohio State jumped out to a 14-0 lead before Oregon scored 38 straight points. Smith went more than two quarters without a catch and was seen yelling toward the sideline, which led one Ohio State reporter to call him “a petulant child” for the outburst. After the game, head coach Ryan Day said that “there needs to be accountability” and that it starts with the coaching staff. The loss dropped the Buckeyes to 6-3, their first three-loss season under Day. item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim and Hannover share the points in four-goal thriller
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim and Hannover share the points in four-goal thriller The visitors made the brighter start and came close to opening the scoring inside the opening 15 minutes. Benjamin Källman did well to get in behind the Heidenheim defence before pulling the ball back for Husseyn Chakroun, who somehow missed the target with the goal at his mercy. Hannover continued to look dangerous, with Marcel Hartel and Stefán Teitur Thórdarson also threatening, while Heidenheim struggled to create much of note in the opening stages. Despite the visitors looking the more likely to score, it was Frank Schmidt’s side who broke the deadlock shortly before half-time. A long-range free-kick from Paul Hennrich caused problems inside the Hannover penalty area, with Jean Hugonet inadvertently diverting the ball into the path of Tim Siersleben, who reacted quickest to head home from close range in the 43rd minute. Heidenheim therefore went into the interval with a somewhat fortunate 1-0 advantage, despite Hannover having created the better opportunities during the opening 45 minutes. Sandro Wagner’s side came out with renewed purpose after the restart and were rewarded for their efforts in the 55th minute. Källman picked out Thórdarson on the edge of the penalty area, with the midfielder producing a precise first-time finish into the bottom-right corner to bring Hannover level. The visitors continued to build momentum and completed the turnaround just eight minutes later. Marcel Hartel delivered a dangerous corner into the penalty area, where Hugonet rose highest to power a header beyond Thomas Dähne and put Hannover 2-1 ahead in the 63rd minute. However, their advantage lasted less than three minutes. Heidenheim responded through a corner of their own, with substitute Christian Conteh delivering an inviting ball towards the near post for Budu Zivzivadze to glance a header into the net and restore parity at 2-2. Both sides subsequently pushed for a winner in an increasingly open encounter. Hannover continued to threaten through Chakroun, while Heidenheim looked to take advantage of their attacking momentum following the equaliser. Neither side could find a decisive breakthrough during the closing stages, however, with the points ultimately shared after an entertaining afternoon in Heidenheim. The result extends Heidenheim’s winless run, while Hannover will take encouragement from their second-half response after coming from behind to take the lead, even if they were unable to hold on for all three points.

item.title: Messi Makes History, Back-to-Back MLS Golden Boot Wins
item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; a fan holds up a Inter Miami CF forward Lionel Messi (10) sign during a game against Charlotte FC at Nu Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Lionel Messi has become the first player in Major League Soccer history to win back-to-back Golden Boot awards . The Inter Miami forward finished the 2026 regular season with a league-high 26 goals, according to ESPN . This feat separates him from every other striker in the league’s short history. At 39 years old, Messi is not just scoring; he is dominating the statistical landscape while others struggle to keep pace. The numbers tell the whole story without any need for hype. Messi recorded 26 goals in 31 appearances (29 starts). He also added 17 assists, giving him a total of 43 goal contributions for the season. This massive output came despite a disappointing 3-3 draw with Charlotte FC in his final regular-season game on Saturday. Miami surrendered a three-goal lead in that match, but the result did not change Messi’s standing. He finished four clear of his nearest rival, FC Dallas forward Petar Musa. Respect Earned Through Work Talent gets you on the field, but consistency keeps you there. Messi has now been the top scorer in multiple MLS regular seasons, a feat only six players have ever achieved. His coach, Cristian “Kily” González, sees the effort behind the stats. González also noted that “None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues.” This respect is not just talk. In 2025, Messi secured the Golden Boot by netting 29 goals across only 28 matches. He followed that up with 26 goals this year. Inter Miami advanced to second place in the Eastern Conference thanks to his efforts. The team clinched a playoff spot and secured a ticket to the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup, their fourth straight time. Messi is now the front-runner to win the league MVP award again, having already won it in 2024 and 2025. Rivalry Records and Playoff Stakes While Messi claimed the individual title, the team battle saw a different outcome. Following a 2-0 Saturday victory over FC Cincinnati, Nashville SC established a new MLS single-season points record of 77. “It’s a massive achievement for the club, for us as players, and yeah, it’s going to go down in history, and I think that was the message before the game,” Surridge said. Nashville also set records for most wins and fewest losses. Inter Miami finished with 60 points, well behind Nashville’s total but enough for the second seed. The seventh-seeded Columbus Crew will face Miami in a best-of-three first-round playoff series where Miami holds home-field advantage.

There was a variety of opinions from Austin FC fans Saturday about what the club needs to do in the offseason to be better next year, but all of them said one thing needs to happen more often in 2027: Winning . Austin FC finished out its season with a 2-0 loss to Portland at Q2 Stadium, and while the Timbers needed the three points to reach the MLS playoffs - they actually rose to seventh in the West to avoid the play-in game - it was a meaningless contest for the Verde and Black. item.title: There May Be Fewer $100 Million Contracts Offered In MLB Free Agency
item.description: Tarik Skubal is far and away the best free agent on the market this off-season. (Photo by Nicole Vasquez/MLB Photos via Getty Images) MLB Photos via Getty Images By all accounts, the 2026-27 Major League Baseball free agent class is pretty weak . There is one headliner: two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. His impending free agency was the talk of baseball all summer, as his original team, the Detroit Tigers, had to decide if they were going to keep him and risk losing him for only a compensation pick (if he stayed, Detroit would have made him a qualifying offer), or trade him for long-term assets. The club waited as long as they could, but in the end, they took the two ( actually three ) in the bush, and sent the lefty to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the trade deadline. Skubal is predicted to make anywhere from $352 million ( Kiley McDaniel, ESPN ), to $405 million ( Tim Britton, The Athletic ), to $425 million ( MLB Trade Rumors ). You can find all sorts of other guesses on various websites. Suffice it to say, Skubal will get paid. But what about everyone else? Since the 2014-15 off-season, 64 free agents have received nine-figure contracts. That is an average of just more than five per year. What will this year’s tally be? First off, there is the question of how willing owners will be to commit extraordinary sums on the eve of a lockout and with the future financial system of the game totally unknown. However, the owners acknowledged that any salary cap would need to be phased in, so they may take this opportunity to sign big contracts such that they may be “grandfathered” in to the new collective bargaining agreement. But, there just are not that many players in this year’s free agency pool worthy of those types of deals. And yet, if the owners get their way with a salary cap, they will also have to contend with a salary floor, which means that at least 15 of them will be required to increase (in some cases, substantially) their payroll. All of which begs the question: how many nine-figure deals will be signed between now and midnight December 1 st or immediately after the lockout ends and players need to report to (an abridged) spring training? The aforementioned Tim Britton thinks we will hit the average, with five players getting at least $100 million. He predicts Adrián Morejón will get five years, $110 million; Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki will each get four years, $108 million; and the latest Japanese star, Teruaki Sato, will pull in five years and $105 million. Kiley McDaniel of ESPN is considerably less optimistic, as he believes that – other than Skubal – only Sato will cross the nine-figure threshold, with five years and $115 million. item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Bochum snatch dramatic late victory over Karlsruher SC
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Bochum snatch dramatic late victory over Karlsruher SC The hosts made an electric start and needed just six minutes to take the lead. Berkan Taz picked out Christian Rasmussen on the left-hand side of the penalty area, with the Danish forward taking aim and firing a superb effort into the far corner beyond Hans Christian Bernat. However, Karlsruhe responded almost immediately. Just two minutes later, Marvin Wanitzek teed up Kevin Wiethaup on the edge of the penalty area, and the midfielder produced an equally impressive finish into the top corner to restore parity. Bochum subsequently enjoyed more possession and looked the more threatening side, with Karol Mets going closest to restoring their advantage. The defender was unable to convert from close range after Philipp Hofmann had nodded the ball into his path, while Jarne Steuckers also tested Bernat with a powerful effort from outside the box. Despite the hosts’ pressure, Karlsruhe remained organised and managed to keep the score level heading into the interval. The visitors made a flying start to the second half and took the lead just five minutes after the restart. Following a Bochum corner, Shio Fukuda helped keep the ball alive before Tim Civeja spotted Timo Horn off his line and produced a sensational strike from around the halfway line, sending the ball over the goalkeeper and into the net to make it 2-1. Bochum responded almost immediately, however, with Hofmann bringing the hosts level in the 53rd minute. After Taz delivered the ball into the penalty area, Rasmussen helped it into the path of the former Karlsruhe striker, who made no mistake from close range. Both sides subsequently searched for a winner, with Bochum coming particularly close through Taz and Hofmann in the 74th minute. Bernat initially parried Taz’s effort before producing an outstanding reaction save to deny Hofmann from the rebound. The Karlsruhe goalkeeper continued to frustrate the hosts as the game entered its closing stages, while Bochum also had to remain alert to the visitors’ counter-attacking threat. However, Uwe Rösler’s side eventually found their breakthrough in the second minute of stoppage time. After Mansour Ouro-Tagba drove forward down the left, Hofmann helped the ball back into the path of Taz, whose effort was saved by Bernat. The resulting attack remained alive, and Karol Mets delivered the decisive ball into the penalty area for Hofmann to finish from close range and complete a remarkable comeback. The late winner sparked celebrations around the Vonovia Ruhrstadion, with Bochum claiming all three points in an entertaining five-goal encounter. The victory continues Bochum’s recent improvement under Rösler, while Karlsruhe will be left frustrated after twice taking the lead and ultimately coming away empty-handed.

item.title: Zigiotti Olme strike helps Man Utd to win at Villa
item.description: Women's Super League Aston Villa 0 - 1 Manchester United FT Manchester United are fourth in the WSL table [Press Association] Julia Zigiotti Olme stepped off the bench to seal a 1-0 Women's Super League win for Manchester United against Aston Villa at Villa Park. United limited Villa to just two touches in their box in the first half, but could not turn their dominance into a lead. The hosts came to life after half-time before Swedish substitute Zigiotti Olme scored an unmarked header to decide the game in the 72nd minute. The win extends United's unbeaten WSL run to seven games, while Brian Sorensen lost his first league game since his appointment as Villa coach in September. United failed to take advantage of a one-sided first half in which they forced Villa keeper Akane Okuma to make five saves. She was beaten for United's best chance as Hinata Miyazawa's speculative effort from 20 yards struck the crossbar. Meanwhile, Sorensen waited until the 45th minute to see his side have their first attempt at goal, as Lucia Kendall's strike was easily held by Phallon Tullis-Joyce. The American goalkeeper kept an invigorated Villa side at bay after the break, making impressive saves to keep out Amalie Vangsgaard and Oriane Jean-Francois. Having scored a combined five of United's nine league goals this season, Zigiotti Olme and Andrea Medina were swapped out of the starting line-up at Villa, as Eva Olid cited rotation and Medina's illness. Both came off the bench and were involved in United's winner. Marauding forward with the ball at her feet, Medina occupied two Villa players before slipping the ball to Hanna Lundkvist. With a deep cross, the Swede found compatriot Zigiotti Olme who nodded the ball unchallenged into the Villa net. Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

item.title: “Don’t Think Sam Leavitt Is the One”: LSU Legend Delivers Harsh Verdict on Lane Kiffin’s QB After Alabama Blowout
item.description: Sam Leavitt © Reuters Lane Kiffin’s first season at LSU is turning into a frustrating campaign, and the Tigers’ latest defeat has even led some of the program’s biggest legends to question the team’s direction. After a disappointing 31-13 home loss to Alabama, former LSU running back Leonard Fournette delivered a brutal assessment of quarterback Sam Leavitt and the team’s overall performance. Speaking on “4th and South” alongside former LSU teammate Jarvis Landry, Fournette did not hold back his frustration with what he witnessed against the Crimson Tide. “I’m so disappointed. The truth is, I don’t think Sam Leavitt is the one,” Fournette said. LSU struggled to turn promising offensive numbers into points. Despite Leavitt throwing for 380 yards, the Tigers managed only 13 points, with an interception and several failed fourth-down attempts proving costly. Fournette also questioned the team’s lack of swagger and the offensive approach under Kiffin. “This ain’t us. Go find y’all a running back,” Fournette said. He also expressed frustration with the team’s running back usage, asking why players such as Caden Durham, Harlem Berry and Dilin Jones weren’t getting more opportunities. He also pointed to Alabama’s defensive coach talking trash on the sideline, suggesting the Tigers were being pushed around in their own stadium. Landry shared his former teammate’s frustration, describing the performance as embarrassing. He also suggested Leavitt appeared to be playing through an injury, raising questions about whether the quarterback was fully healthy. Leavitt previously suffered a hamstring injury in LSU’s matchup against Texas A&M, and Kiffin confirmed the issue. LSU’s Playoff Hopes Take Another Hit After Alabama Defeat Saturday’s numbers explain why Fournette and Landry were so disappointed. LSU converted just five of 14 third downs and failed on all four fourth-down attempts. The Tigers also managed only 77 rushing yards on 33 carries, averaging a disappointing 2.3 yards per attempt. Leavitt completed 35 of 47 passes for 380 yards , but his late-first-half interception kept LSU from adding points before the break. Kiffin acknowledged the mistake, calling it a poor decision while speaking to ABC. “We have to do a better job against blitz zero down there. Obviously, Sam made a poor decision there, and we’re in field goal range (there),” he said. Meanwhile, Skip Bayless took a shot at Kiffin’s expensive contract, joking that LSU would want a refund on the seven-year, $91 million deal. “LSU is going to want a refund,” he wrote on X. Now sitting at 6-3, the Tigers have little room for further setbacks if they hope to play in the postseason. Their next opportunity to respond comes against Texas.
